So we built a different kind of trip. Fewer places, longer stays. Early starts when the light is good and the paths are empty, long afternoons with nothing on the schedule. Nights in inns where the owner remembers your name, and dinners that follow whatever the hills and the sea are offering that week.
So we go early, go late, or go next door. A temple at 7am, a neighbouring valley instead of the famous one, a weekday instead of a Saturday. It makes more difference than you would think.

So we try to be good guests. We go to fewer places for longer, at the quiet ends of the day. We work with local guides and family-run inns, and spread what you spend across towns that welcome it. We respect closures and photography rules without argument. And we only travel in small, private groups.
